title: Calibrated abstention to eliminate confident hallucination in LLMs
description: Large language models answer questions fluently even when they lack the underlying knowledge, producing confident but fabricated answers (hallucinations). As of the source work, no method lets a model reliably recognize the boundary of its own knowledge and abstain ('I don't know') in a way that is calibrated to its actual likelihood of being correct - without degrading helpfulness on questions it can answer, and without relying on external retrieval or a separate verifier model.
canonical_description: no method gives an LLM calibrated self-knowledge to abstain on out-of-knowledge questions without external tools

evidence.quote: Whether a model can be made to abstain in a manner calibrated to its true knowledge boundaries, without an external verifier, remains an open question.
